quest.title: Threefold Expectations
quest.description: The teapot troubles are still causing Uncle Luo quite the headache...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back, Uncle Luo!

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Ohh, thank you! The tea cauldron technician has already arrived and is tinkering with it over there.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: *sigh* I wonder what's gone wrong with it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Err... So what's she doing?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Eh, I don't understand the technician's jargon either. Structural analysis this, bond graph that... Anyway, she's examining the tea cauldron.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, over there...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Before long, Hautemontagne finishes the examination...

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: Mr. Luo! I've finished examining the tea cauldron. From the look of it...

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: Eh? You two are back!?

choices.text: I was worried about the tea cauldron.

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: Haha, no need to worry. There's no such thing as a problem that can't be solved, after all!

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: So, how's it looking? What's wrong with the tea cauldron?

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: It's not so much the tea cauldron itself, as... Well, take a look at the bond graph I've sketched out over here.

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: The flow source itself should be fine, but something's off with the performance of several gyrators over here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Flow... What now? Paimon's totally perplexed!

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: Ahaha... Apologies! I'm just so used to using all these technical terms...

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: In layman's terms, the tea cauldron itself is probably fine, but there's something wrong with three of the connected mechanisms. This is causing the flow of elemental energy nearby to act a little funny.

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: Hmph, I knew it! Grandpa Lu insisted the problem wasn't with the tea cauldron, but the soil...

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: Three mechanisms... Oh, right! You say "mechanisms," we say "monoliths"! Mountain Ley Lines wind all over the place, so you have to control them with sacred stones to prevent chaotic elemental energy...

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: Hmm... Chaotic elemental energy is indeed a terrifying thing, but these mechanisms... shouldn't have much to do with the Ley Lines. They aren't directly connected.

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: While we can't clearly see how the mechanisms are structured, their operating principles are the same! Those legendary adepti must have been phenomenal artisans!

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: Hehe, you're not wrong there! I may not understand the mechanical mysteries at work here... But that Cloud Retainer sure is an incredible adeptus for having come up with such ingenuity!

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: These "monoliths"... Functionally speaking, a more accurate name would be "Three-Phase Asynchronous Elemental Tuners."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Tuners?

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: That's right! According to the records, the great master Alain Guillotin himself — founder of the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering — also designed a constrained layer dampener to regulate the elemental energy.

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: While his blueprints are long lost, the principle should be the same... Emphasis on "should" be!

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: Haha... Shame I'm too old to learn such things. So, let me ask again, what caused this problem? Is it serious, and can it be fixed?

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: Us technicians don't get too concerned with whether a problem is serious or not! We only think about whether or not it can be fixed. As for this particular issue... Let's just say if it wasn't fixable, I'd have left a long time ago!

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: Haha, well that's a relief! There I was, thinking the adepti saw us as a bunch of neglectful fools, and had cast some kind of magic on this ward to make it irreparable!

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: Mr. Luo, all devices are fundamentally the same! If they're left for too long without being maintained or repaired, it's only natural that problems will arise!

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: As Master Guillotin once said — no matter what the system, or how ingenious the original design, all mechanisms will eventually collapse if left to run completely on their own!

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: If there's actually something wrong with the tea cauldron, it would be totally unreasonable to blame the soil for not producing quality tea leaves without addressing the root of the problem!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Hmm, Fujin did mention earlier that the reason why the tea doesn't taste so great is because of the soil and water. If that "tuner" could be fixed, then maybe the water and soil will improve too...)

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: Anyway, the three mechanisms connected to the tea cauldron aren't too far from here, so let me go tinker about a bit, and I should be able to fix them!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll come help too.

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: Thanks, that's very kind of you! In that case, there's no point waiting around — let's get going!

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: #Haha... Excellent! {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Paimon, I'll leave this tea cauldron business to your good selves and the technician!

choices.text: Don't get worked up, Uncle Luo...

response.speaker: Hautemontagne
response.text: Mr. Luo is basically right. These mechanisms were specially designed to prevent chaotic elemental energy, but they have nothing to do with Ley Lines...

choices.text: I was worried about the tea.
So that's real qinggong in action, eh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Err, pretty sure that's not what that is...

talks.objective: Help Mountain adjust the three Monoliths

dialogues.speaker: Hautemontagne
dialogues.text: Mmhmm, seems like there's nothing wrong with the elemental reaction here. Why don't we try...

talks.objective: Help Mountain adjust the three Monoliths

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: From what that technician lass said, it seems like there's a problem with the monoliths in the mountains...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: *sigh* But I don't know exactly how serious the problem is. I just hope it can be fixed quickly...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uncle Luo! With Mountain's help, all three mechanisms have now been taken care of!

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Haha, I knew you three could do it! Such extraordinary skill!

dialogues.speaker: Hautemontagne
dialogues.text: #It was all thanks to {NICKNAME} and Paimon! I just need to do some final checks now, though there shouldn't be any problems... You two wouldn't be able to help out again, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, let's head up together!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You follow Hautemontagne to the tea cauldron...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After tapping the tea cauldron lightly, a slight look of surprise appears on Hautemontagne's face...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh, what's up?

dialogues.speaker: Hautemontagne
dialogues.text: Hmm, there's just something strange about the echo. According to my calculations, it should be more of a "thump—thump—thump" sound...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you have miscalculated, maybe?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Surely that's way too abstract, anyway! What do you mean by "thump—thump—thump"!?

dialogues.speaker: Hautemontagne
dialogues.text: Well... The tea cauldron's empty, so going by the formula left by Master Guillotin, the echo should be much clearer! What in Teyvat could be the reason...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What exactly is the problem? Can't see anything from the outside...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: *taps the tea cauldron* Like this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... No response?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: *taps the tea cauldron* Or like this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still no respo... Wahhhh!

choices.text: Why don't you take a look inside, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't fit in there! No way, surely!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon feels like we've discussed this before, but... Why do you always try to get Paimon to go into such strange places!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Forget it! I'll check it out myself...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Whoa, how did you come out from there? I was just about to call someone — I was worried sick! Never imagined an adepti treasure could suck people in like that...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: But check this out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! There's tea flowing out after cleaning out the elemental sedimentation... Hang on, this looks like it's just regular water!

dialogues.speaker: Hautemontagne
dialogues.text: Wow... Liyue's adepti mechanisms are truly incredible. They can even generate whole new spaces! Even Master Guillotin himself couldn't do such a thing...

dialogues.speaker: Hautemontagne
dialogues.text: Seems like Little Mao was right, after all! "There'll always be someone better than you, and teapots you haven't been to"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's not how it goes!

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Needless to say, without you the tea cauldron wouldn't have been repaired so quickly. Thanks for your help, Haut... mon... uh...?

dialogues.speaker: Hautemontagne
dialogues.text: Hautemontagne! But you don't have to use my full name. Just call me Mountain — it basically means the same thing anyway!

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Haha! Alright, well thank you, Mountain.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: This'll sort out the soil issue too... Hmph, guess you lost the bet, Grandpa Lu!

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Can't let you young'uns toil away and go hungry for nothing... Once the current tea crisis has been resolved, we'll all finally be able to breathe a little easier, and no longer have to worry about losses...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Grandpa Lu, Laoding, and Xiaoding hadn't slept a wink for several nights, worrying about the substandard tea. But now the tea cauldron's been repaired... Just you wait and see! I hope I'm right, anyway!

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Thank you all, dear guests, for your help as well. Qiaoying Village's future is looking bright once again!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, you're too kind! As long as there's plenty of tea and snacks waiting for us the next time we come!

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: But of course, that goes without saying! You're Qiaoying Village VIPs now. Once the first batch is done, I'll reserve some of the very highest quality tea for you to sample!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uncle Luo! With Mountain's help, all three mechanisms have now been taken care of!

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: Haha, we'll invite the tourists to experience our centuries-old tea making traditions themselves... And pocket a few Mora for entry tickets in exchange...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph, seems like someone's forgotten to respect the adepti...
